newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi governor's aide defends education veto.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi governor's aide defends education veto.

text.p: Although the Mississippi Legislature overrode Gov. Kirk Fordice's veto of the state's education funding reform bill, there was "a significant amount of support" for the governor's decision, his press spokesman said Thursday.
"Any good steward of taxpayer dollars would have vetoed that bill," said Heath Hall, Fordice's press spokesman.

The House voted 83-37 and the Senate voted 35-15 Wednesday to override the veto. The override required at least 80 votes in the House and 34 in the Senate, so it passed by only four votes, Hall pointed out.
"There was a significant amount of support for Gov. Fordice's decision," Hall said. "There's a significant amount of concern out there for this bill."

The bill uses general fund surpluses and new revenues to raise school spending between $12 million and $26 million a year for six years. It sets a per-pupil minimum for spending, with the state subsidizing districts that cannot meet that level.
It also allows school districts to assume up to $160 per student in new bond debt without a referendum before June 30, 1998, with the state guaranteeing the bonds.
Fordice said the measure relied too heavily on economic growth that may not continue and could have encouraged districts to issue too much debt.
He proposed an altenative plan that would have frozen the base cost, minimizing the risk to taxpayers. His plan would have added accountability and local oversight provisions for bond debt.
Heath described Fordice's alternative plan as "a good faith effort by the governor to address the importance of equity in school funding."
